# Commands

`gh-touchid help` lists every command; `gh-touchid help <command>` or `gh-touchid <command> --help` shows one, with an
example. Everything after `gh-touchid gh` goes to GitHub CLI, so `gh-touchid gh --help` is GitHub CLI's help.

Each command takes its input as flags and arguments, or with `--input <file|->` as one JSON object; `rpc` and `mcp` take
the same object as a call's arguments. The Input tables name its keys: on the command line a key is the flag of the same
name in kebab case (`client_id` is `--client-id`; `open_browser` false is `--no-open`), or the argument the usage shows
in its place. With `--json` the output is one JSON object, which the Output tables describe; a failure ends stderr with
an [error code](errors.md). The annotations are MCP's tool hints. See [Scripts and agents](scripting.md) for `--json`,
`--input`, `rpc` and `mcp`.

| Usage | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`gh-touchid app create <owner> [--name <name>] [--no-open] [--git-setup\|--no-git-setup]`](#app-create) | Create an owner's GitHub App |
| [`gh-touchid app add <owner> --client-id <client-id> [--no-open] [--git-setup\|--no-git-setup] < client-secret`](#app-add) | Add an App made by hand |
| [`gh-touchid app login <owner> [--no-open]`](#app-login) | Sign in to an owner's App again |
| [`gh-touchid app remove <owner> [--yes]`](#app-remove) | Remove an owner's App |
| [`gh-touchid account add <login> < token`](#account-add) | Store a token of one of your accounts |
| [`gh-touchid account remove <login>`](#account-remove) | Delete a stored account token |
| [`gh-touchid reader create [--name <name>] [--no-open]`](#reader-create) | Create the reader |
| [`gh-touchid reader add --app-id <app-id> < private-key`](#reader-add) | Add the reader's key |
| [`gh-touchid reader remove [--yes]`](#reader-remove) | Remove the reader |
| [`gh-touchid gh <arguments...>`](#gh) | Run GitHub CLI with a narrowed token |
| [`gh-touchid git setup <owner>`](#git-setup) | Make Git ask gh-touchid for an owner |
| [`gh-touchid git credential <get\|store\|erase>`](#git-credential) | Git's credential helper |
| [`gh-touchid as <login> [--] <command> [arguments...]`](#as) | Run a command as one of your accounts |
| [`gh-touchid session [--repo <repo>]... [--cwd <cwd>]`](#session) | Register the calling program as a session |
| [`gh-touchid elevate --for <for> [--repo <repo>]... [--cwd <cwd>]`](#elevate) | Let tokens include workflows for a while |
| [`gh-touchid status`](#status) | What is stored and set up |
| [`gh-touchid setup [<owners>...]`](#setup) | Set up what is missing |
| [`gh-touchid lock`](#lock) | End every session approval and elevation |
| [`gh-touchid version`](#version) | gh-touchid's version |
| [`gh-touchid help [<command>]`](#help) | Print every command's usage, or one command's |
| [`gh-touchid rpc`](#rpc) | Serve the operations over JSON-RPC |
| [`gh-touchid mcp`](#mcp) | Serve the operations as an MCP server |

## app create

```sh
gh-touchid app create <owner> [--name <name>] [--no-open] [--git-setup|--no-git-setup]
```

`app create` makes a private GitHub App for an owner from a manifest in your browser (named &lt;owner>-touchid unless
--name says otherwise), signs you in to it and opens its installation page (--no-open prints the first URL instead). It
asks for Touch ID before storing anything.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid app create acme --name acme-agents
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git_setup` | boolean | no | Set up Git for the owner afterwards. Without it, a terminal is asked; otherwise Git is left as is. |
| `name` | string | no | The App's name. |
| `open_browser` | boolean | no | Open the browser (default true); false prints the address instead. |
| `owner` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | string | The App's slug. |
| `app_id` | integer | The App's ID. |
| `git_setup` | boolean | Whether Git was set up for the owner. |
| `install_url` | string | Where to install it. |
| `login` | string | Who is signed in to it. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## app add

```sh
gh-touchid app add <owner> --client-id <client-id> [--no-open] [--git-setup|--no-git-setup] < client-secret
```

`app add` takes an App made by hand: its client ID, and its client secret on stdin or at a hidden prompt; it must list
the callback URL http://127.0.0.1:47911/callback. It signs you in to it and asks for Touch ID before storing both.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid app add acme --client-id Iv23liAbCdEf < client-secret
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client_id` | string | yes | The App's client ID. |
| `client_secret` | string | yes | The App's client secret. Secret: read from stdin only. |
| `git_setup` | boolean | no | Set up Git for the owner afterwards. Without it, a terminal is asked; otherwise Git is left as is. |
| `open_browser` | boolean | no | Open the browser (default true); false prints the address instead. |
| `owner` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | string or null | The App's slug, when it is installed where you can see. |
| `git_setup` | boolean | Whether Git was set up for the owner. |
| `login` | string | Who is signed in to it. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

| `owner` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |

## app remove

```sh
gh-touchid app remove <owner> [--yes]
```

`app remove` deletes the owner's App and your sign-in from this Mac and the owner's Git entries, ends the sign-in's
grant on GitHub, and prints where to delete the App on GitHub. It asks on a terminal; elsewhere --yes confirms.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid app remove acme --yes
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `yes` | boolean | no | Confirm without asking. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delete_url` | string or null | Where to delete the App on GitHub. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `removed` | object |  |

## account add

```sh
gh-touchid account add <login> < token
```

`account add` stores a token of one of your GitHub accounts (hidden input or stdin) once GitHub confirms its login,
after Touch ID. `as` uses it.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid account add alice < token
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `token` | string | yes | A token of the account. Secret: read from stdin only. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `login` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `scopes` | string or null | The scopes GitHub lists for the token. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## account remove

```sh
gh-touchid account remove <login>
```

`account remove` deletes the stored token of one of your accounts.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid account remove alice
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `login` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `removed` | boolean | Always true: a missing token is an error. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive yes · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## reader create

```sh
gh-touchid reader create [--name <name>] [--no-open]
```

`reader create` makes the reader: a GitHub App of yours with no permissions, installed on your user account with no
repository, whose tokens let gh read public data without Touch ID for owners without an App and outside any repository.
The browser makes the App on GitHub; one Touch ID stores it; then the browser installs it and gh-touchid checks it with
one token, revoked at once. Refused while a reader is stored.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid reader create
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | no | The App's name on GitHub; by default gh-touchid-reader-&lt;6 hex digits>. |
| `open_browser` | boolean | no | Open the browser (default true); false prints the address. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | string | The reader App's slug; it acts as &lt;slug>[bot]. |
| `app_id` | integer, at least 1 | The reader App's ID. |
| `install_url` | string | GitHub's page for installing the reader. |
| `installed` | boolean | Whether GitHub lists its installation, checked with a token. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | The user account the reader belongs to and is installed on. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## reader add

```sh
gh-touchid reader add --app-id <app-id> < private-key
```

`reader add` stores a reader App made by hand, or a new key for the stored one: the App's private key (the PKCS#1 .pem
GitHub downloads) on stdin. GitHub must confirm the App ID, that the App belongs to a user and has no permissions, and
one installation on that user with no repository; then one Touch ID stores it, replacing any reader. Prints the key's
fingerprint, and the replaced key's with where to delete it on GitHub.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid reader add --app-id 123456 < gh-touchid-reader.private-key.pem
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | integer, at least 1 | yes | The App ID, from the App's settings on GitHub. |
| `private_key` | string | no | The App's private key, PKCS#1 PEM (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY); on the command line, piped to stdin. Secret: read from stdin only. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | string | The reader App's slug. |
| `app_id` | integer, at least 1 | The reader App's ID. |
| `fingerprint` | string | The stored key's fingerprint, as GitHub shows it. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | The user account the reader belongs to and is installed on. |
| `replaced` | object | The key this one replaced, when a reader was stored. |

<details>
<summary>The fields within <code>replaced</code> (JSON Schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "replaced": {
    "additionalProperties": false,
    "description": "The key this one replaced, when a reader was stored.",
    "properties": {
      "delete_keys_url": {
        "description": "Where the replaced key is deleted on GitHub.",
        "type": "string"
      },
      "fingerprint": {
        "description": "The replaced key's fingerprint.",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "fingerprint",
      "delete_keys_url"
    ],
    "type": "object"
  }
}
```

</details>

Annotations: read-only no · destructive yes · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## reader remove

```sh
gh-touchid reader remove [--yes]
```

`reader remove` deletes the stored reader, after a yes on the terminal or with --yes; gh then refuses owners without an
App. The App stays on GitHub until deleted at the printed address.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid reader remove --yes
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yes` | boolean | no | Remove without asking. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delete_url` | string | Where the reader App is deleted on GitHub. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `removed` | boolean | Whether a reader was stored and is now deleted. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive yes · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## gh

```sh
gh-touchid gh <arguments...>
```

`gh` runs GitHub CLI with a token for one repository: the one named with -R/--repo, for `gh api` the one its endpoint
names, for `gh repo view OWNER/REPO` and the like their argument, else GH_REPO, else the current repository's origin; a
GraphQL query is not read, so if gh fails with a token taken that way, a notice names its repository and what to set
instead. The token acts as you through the owner's App and lacks the workflows permission unless the repository is
elevated; outside a session, each use asks for Touch ID. With no repository, or for an owner without an App, it uses the
public reader when one is stored (no Touch ID, public data only), and otherwise refuses before asking. Everything after
`gh` goes to GitHub CLI: `gh-touchid gh --help` is its help. With --json, its output is captured.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid gh -R acme/widgets pr list
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `argv` | array of string | yes | GitHub CLI's arguments. |
| `cwd` | string | no | The folder to run in; by default the current one. |
| `stdin` | string | no | GitHub CLI's standard input (with --json); by default none. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exit_code` | integer | The command's exit status (128 plus the signal that ended it). |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `stderr` | string | Its standard error, when at most 1 MiB. |
| `stderr_file` | string | The 0600 file holding its standard error, when larger. |
| `stdout` | string | Its standard output, when at most 1 MiB. |
| `stdout_file` | string | The 0600 file holding its standard output, when larger. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## git setup

```sh
gh-touchid git setup <owner>
```

`git setup` makes this gh-touchid the only credential helper Git asks for the owner's repositories, in your global Git
configuration (write the owner as in your remotes' URLs).

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid git setup acme
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` | array of string | The section's entries as written. |
| `file` | string | The configuration file written. |
| `helper` | string | The helper entry naming this gh-touchid. |
| `kept` | integer, at least 0 | How many other settings of the section were kept. |
| `notes` | array of string | Advice about what may still change these entries. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `owner` | string | A GitHub user or organization. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## git credential

```sh
gh-touchid git credential <get|store|erase>
```

`git credential` is the helper `git setup` names; it answers only Git's HTTPS transport, in Git's key=value form, never
to a terminal, --json or --input.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid git credential get
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | one of `"get"`, `"store"`, `"erase"` | yes | What Git asks. |
| `host` | string | yes | The URL's host. |
| `path` | string | no | The URL's path: owner/name.git. |
| `protocol` | string | yes | The URL's scheme. |
| `username` | string | no | The user name Git has. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `password` | string | The token. Secret. |
| `password_expiry_utc` | integer | When the token expires, in Unix seconds. |
| `username` | string | Who the token acts as. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## as

```sh
gh-touchid as <login> [--] <command> [arguments...]
```

`as` runs a command as one of your stored accounts, with Touch ID on every use, sessions included: `as <login> gh ...`
runs GitHub CLI with that account's token, anything else runs with GH_TOUCHID_AS=&lt;login>, which gh and Git honour.
The `--` before the command is optional. With --json, its output is captured.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid as alice -- gh issue create -R octo-org/hello-world
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `argv` | array of string | yes | The command and its arguments. |
| `cwd` | string | no | The folder to run in; by default the current one. |
| `login` | string | yes | A GitHub user or organization. |
| `stdin` | string | no | The command's standard input (with --json); by default none. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exit_code` | integer | The command's exit status (128 plus the signal that ended it). |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `stderr` | string | Its standard error, when at most 1 MiB. |
| `stderr_file` | string | The 0600 file holding its standard error, when larger. |
| `stdout` | string | Its standard output, when at most 1 MiB. |
| `stdout_file` | string | The 0600 file holding its standard output, when larger. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world yes.

## session

```sh
gh-touchid session [--repo <repo>]... [--cwd <cwd>]
```

`session` registers the program that ran it (looking past shells that only run a command or a script). Its first GitHub
use asks for Touch ID once; then it and everything it starts get tokens for its repositories without Touch ID until it
exits, and issue-only tokens for other repositories your Apps are installed on (public ones ask per use). Without --repo
it takes the outermost Git repository here and those nested up to two levels below it whose owner has an App.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid session --repo acme/widgets
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cwd` | string | no | The folder to run in; by default the current one. |
| `repos` | array of string | no | Repositories; without them, those of the working folder. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `program` | string | The registered program, as program[pid]. |
| `repositories` | array of string | The session's repositories. |
| `state` | one of `"approved"`, `"pending"` | Whether it is approved yet. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent no · open-world no.

## elevate

```sh
gh-touchid elevate --for <for> [--repo <repo>]... [--cwd <cwd>]
```

`elevate` lets tokens for the repositories (without --repo, the current one) include the workflows permission for a
while: 30m, 8h, 1h30m, at most 1d. It asks for Touch ID.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid elevate --for 30m --repo acme/widgets
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cwd` | string | no | The folder to run in; by default the current one. |
| `for` | string | yes | How long: 30m, 8h, 1h30m, 1d. |
| `repos` | array of string | no | Repositories; without them, those of the working folder. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `repositories` | array of string | The elevated repositories. |
| `until` | string | When the elevation ends, ISO 8601. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive no · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## status

```sh
gh-touchid status
```

`status` lists stored Apps with who is signed in to each, your accounts, the public reader, whether Git goes through
this gh-touchid for each owner, which `gh` comes first on PATH (and how to put this gh-touchid's first), whether another
gh is signed in, and sessions and elevations. It reads no secret.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid status --json
```

Input: none.

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accounts` | array of object | Your accounts with a stored token. |
| `agent` | string or null | What keeps the agent from being used. |
| `apps` | array of object | Owners with a stored App. |
| `elevations` | array of object |  |
| `gh` | object | The gh first on PATH, this installation's wrapper, and the fix when it is not first. |
| `git` | array of object | Git, for each owner with a stored App. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `reader` | object or null | The public reader, null when none is stored. |
| `sessions` | array of object |  |

## setup

```sh
gh-touchid setup [<owners>...]
```

`setup` does what is missing for each owner named (by default each owner with a stored App): creates its App, signs you
in, sets up Git; then stores the public reader unless one is stored, and says whether this gh-touchid's gh comes first
on PATH. Without a terminal, or with --no-input, it does only what needs no browser (Git) and fails listing the commands
for the rest.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid setup acme
```

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owners` | array of string | no | The owners; by default each owner with a stored App. |

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `steps` | array of object |  |

        }

}

## lock

```sh
gh-touchid lock
```

`lock` ends every session approval and elevation now.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid lock
```

Input: none.

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `locked` | boolean | Whether anything was active. |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |

Annotations: read-only no · destructive yes · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## version

```sh
gh-touchid version
```

`version` prints gh-touchid's version.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid version
```

Input: none.

| Output | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notices` | array of string | What gh-touchid tells the caller besides the result, in order: that the reader is in use and must not create or change anything, a token it could not revoke, which repository a failed gh had its token for, a warning. Present only when there is any. |
| `version` | string | The version. |

Annotations: read-only yes · destructive no · idempotent yes · open-world no.

## help

```sh
gh-touchid help [<command>]
```

`help` prints this, or one command's usage; so does `gh-touchid <command> --help`. `gh-touchid --help --json` prints
every operation as an MCP tool, with its input and output schemas, and every command's usage and every error code.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid help gh
```

## rpc

```sh
gh-touchid rpc
```

`rpc` serves the operations as JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin and stdout, one message per line, through gh-touchid-adapter;
approvals still come only from Touch ID, and operations with a secret input are refused there.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid rpc
```

## mcp

```sh
gh-touchid mcp
```

`mcp` serves the operations as an MCP server on stdin and stdout, through gh-touchid-adapter, with the same limits as
`rpc`.

Example:

```sh
gh-touchid mcp
```
